title: Testing the acceptance and effectiveness of an mHealth-supported patient-centered treatment approach for patients with heart failure
summary:
Health behavior and psychological burden such as stress, depression and anxiety have a significant influence on the prognosis and progression of heart failure. This three-arm pilot study is therefore based on mHealth components (apps and sensor devices) that are designed to help patients manage their heart failure. The patients are randomly divided into three groups. One group will use the mHealth components over a period of 3 months. One group will also receive a blended collaborative care intervention, in which a non-physician treatment assistant will be in regular contact with the patients. The third group serves as a control group.
The aim is to investigate how patients experience such an offer and whether it leads to improvements in physical and mental health as well as treatment satisfaction. The long-term goal of the study is to better support patients with heart failure in coping with their disease and establishing a heart-healthy lifestyle.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Consent to data collection
- Willingness to use a smartphone provided by us as part of the study
- Diagnosed heart failure with NYHA class II-III
Exclusion criteria:
- very severe heart failure (NYHA class IV)
- severe mental disorders (e.g. acute psychosis, bipolar disorder or existing addictions, except nicotine)
- Communication barriers (e.g. insufficient knowledge of German to use the app, blindness, deafness)
